scenes.title: Where are we on the map
narration: Have you ever looked at a map of India and wondered about all those colorful shapes?
India is a huge country divided into 28 states and 8 union territories.
Each state has its own special capital city to help manage things. Do you know yours?

scenes.title: What is a capital city
narration: A capital is the main city where the state government works to run things smoothly.
Think of it like the principal's office at your school, where the big decisions happen.
The capital is usually where the Governor lives and where laws are made for the state.

scenes.title: Let us see an example
narration: Let us look at Maharashtra, a large state known for its busy cities and culture.
The capital city of Maharashtra is Mumbai, famous for its grand buildings and the sea.
From Mumbai, the state government looks after millions of people across the whole state.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: Remember, India has 28 states, each with its own capital city for governance.
Capitals are key because they act as the administrative heart of each state.
Think about it: If you could build a new state, what would you name its capital?

scenes.title: Why are they different?
narration: Have you noticed that some places in India are not states, but Union Territories?
These regions are special areas governed directly by the central government in New Delhi.
But why does India have these unique territories instead of making them all states?

scenes.title: Understanding the concept
narration: States have their own elected governments, but Union Territories are managed by the President of India.
The President appoints an administrator or a Lieutenant Governor to look after these areas.
This helps maintain better control over small, strategic, or historically unique regions.

scenes.title: Examples of Territories
narration: Take the capital, Delhi, which is a Union Territory with its own legislative assembly.
Then we have beautiful island groups like the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.
Another example is the coastal region of Puducherry, known for its unique French colonial history.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Union Territories are managed centrally to help with administration and special needs.
In 2024, India has eight Union Territories spread across our diverse country.
If you could visit any Union Territory, which one would you pick and why?

scenes.title: Cities With Nicknames
narration: Many Indian cities have special nicknames. Can you guess why?
A nickname tells us what a city is famous for.
Let us visit some important cities.

scenes.title: North and West
narration: New Delhi is the capital of India, where Parliament meets.
Mumbai is called the financial capital of India and is home to Bollywood.
Jaipur is called the Pink City because of its pink buildings.

scenes.title: South and East
narration: Bengaluru is called the Silicon Valley of India for its computer companies.
Hyderabad is famous for the Charminar, built in 1591.
Kolkata is the City of Joy, with the famous Howrah Bridge.
Chennai has Marina Beach, one of the longest city beaches in the world.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Every city has its own history, food and work.
Nicknames help us remember them.
Think about it: what nickname would you give your town?

scenes.title: Lifelines of India
narration: Rivers give us water to drink, to grow crops and to make electricity.
That is why rivers are called lifelines.
Which is the longest river of India?

scenes.title: Himalayan Rivers
narration: The Ganga is the longest river in India. It starts at the Gangotri glacier.
The Yamuna meets the Ganga at Prayagraj.
The Brahmaputra flows through Assam and is very wide.

scenes.title: Rivers of the South
narration: The Godavari is the longest river of South India and is called Dakshin Ganga.
The Krishna flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
The Narmada flows west and falls into the Arabian Sea.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Ganga is the longest, Godavari is the longest in the south.
We must keep our rivers clean.
Think about it: which river flows nearest to your home?

scenes.title: A Wall Across a River
narration: A dam is a strong wall built across a river.
It stores water in a big lake behind it, called a reservoir.
Why do we build dams?

scenes.title: Uses of Dams
narration: Dams give water to farms through canals.
Falling water turns turbines to make electricity.
Dams also help to control floods.

scenes.title: Famous Dams
narration: The Tehri Dam on the Bhagirathi river is the tallest dam in India.
The Bhakra Nangal Dam is on the Sutlej river.
The Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi is one of the longest dams in the world.
The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built on the Krishna river.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Dams store water, make electricity and control floods.
But dams must be planned carefully to protect people and forests.
Think about it: why do farmers need water all year?

scenes.title: A Wall of Snow
narration: In the north of India stands a giant wall of snowy mountains.
They are the Himalayas, which means home of snow.
Which is the highest peak in India?

scenes.title: Highest Peaks
narration: Mount Everest, about 8,849 metres high, is the highest peak in the world. It is in Nepal.
Kangchenjunga in Sikkim is the highest peak in India.
The Himalayas keep away cold winds and give water to rivers.

scenes.title: Other Mountain Ranges
narration: The Western Ghats run along the west coast.
The Eastern Ghats run along the east coast.
The Aravallis in Rajasthan are among the oldest mountains in the world.
Anamudi in Kerala is the highest peak in South India.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Himalayas in the north, Ghats in the west and east.
Mountains give us rivers, forests and cool weather.
Think about it: would you like to visit the hills or the sea?

scenes.title: A Safe Home for Animals
narration: Where can a tiger live safely, away from hunters?
In a national park, animals and plants are strictly protected.
Hunting and cutting trees are not allowed there.

scenes.title: Famous Parks
narration: Jim Corbett in Uttarakhand, started in 1936, is India's first national park.
Kaziranga in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros.
Gir in Gujarat is the only home of the Asiatic lion in the wild.

scenes.title: More Parks
narration: The Sundarbans in West Bengal have tigers in mangrove forests.
Ranthambore in Rajasthan has tigers near an old fort.
Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh welcomed cheetahs in 2022.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: National parks protect animals in their natural home.
Visitors must stay quiet and never feed the animals.
Think about it: which animal would you like to see in a national park?

scenes.title: A Shelter for Wildlife
narration: A wildlife sanctuary is a place set aside to protect animals and birds.
It is a little like a national park, but some local activities may be allowed.
Many sanctuaries protect birds that fly in from far away.

scenes.title: Bird Sanctuaries
narration: Kolleru Lake in Andhra Pradesh is a sanctuary for pelicans and other water birds.
Ranganathittu in Karnataka has birds nesting on river islands.
Keoladeo in Bharatpur, Rajasthan, began as a bird sanctuary and is now a national park and World Heritage Site.

scenes.title: Why They Matter
narration: Sanctuaries keep endangered animals safe from hunting.
They protect wetlands, forests and grasslands.
Forest guards and scientists watch over the animals.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Sanctuaries give animals and birds a safe home.
We should visit them quietly and keep them clean.
Think about it: why do birds fly to India in winter?

scenes.title: Stories in Stone
narration: Old buildings can tell us stories from long ago.
These special buildings are called monuments.
Let us visit some famous ones.

scenes.title: Delhi and Agra
narration: The Taj Mahal in Agra was built by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
The Red Fort in Delhi is where the Prime Minister hoists the flag on Independence Day.
The Qutub Minar in Delhi is a tall tower started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.

scenes.title: Around India
narration: The Charminar in Hyderabad was built in 1591.
The Sun Temple at Konark in Odisha is shaped like a giant chariot.
The Gateway of India stands by the sea in Mumbai.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Monuments show the skill of builders long ago.
We must not write on them or litter near them.
Think about it: which monument is closest to where you live?

scenes.title: Treasures for the World
narration: Some places are so special that the whole world helps protect them.
UNESCO names them World Heritage Sites.
India has more than 40 such sites.

scenes.title: Cultural Sites
narration: The Ajanta and Ellora caves in Maharashtra have ancient paintings and carvings.
Hampi in Karnataka was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
The Ramappa Temple in Telangana became a World Heritage Site in 2021.

scenes.title: Natural Sites
narration: Kaziranga National Park is a natural heritage site.
The Western Ghats are a heritage site for their amazing plants and animals.
Some sites, like Khangchendzonga National Park, are both natural and cultural.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Heritage sites belong to all people of the world.
We must look after them for children in the future.
Think about it: why should the whole world protect the Taj Mahal?

scenes.title: Many Countries
narration: There are about 195 countries in the world.
Each country has a capital city where its government works.
New Delhi is the capital of India.

scenes.title: Our Neighbours
narration: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.
Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh.
Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.

scenes.title: Around the World
narration: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
Paris is the capital of France.
Canberra, not Sydney, is the capital of Australia.
Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The capital is not always the biggest city.
Learning capitals helps us understand our world.
Think about it: which country would you like to visit, and what is its capital?

scenes.title: Different Money
narration: If you visit another country, can you pay with rupees?
Every country has its own money, called its currency.
We change our money into theirs at a bank or money changer.

scenes.title: Some Currencies
narration: India uses the Indian rupee. Its symbol ₹ was adopted in 2010.
The United States uses the dollar.
Japan uses the yen and the United Kingdom uses the pound sterling.
Many countries in Europe share one currency, the euro.

scenes.title: Our Neighbours
narration: Bangladesh uses the taka.
Nepal and Sri Lanka use their own rupees.
The value of currencies changes every day.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Currency is the money of a country.
₹ rupee, $ dollar, € euro, £ pound, ¥ yen.
Think about it: why do you think each country has its own money?

scenes.title: Big Pieces of Land
narration: The land on Earth is divided into seven huge pieces.
These are called continents.
Can you name the one we live on?

scenes.title: Meet the Continents
narration: Asia is the largest continent. India is in Asia.
Africa has the Sahara desert and the Nile river.
North America and South America are joined by a thin strip of land.

scenes.title: More Continents
narration: Europe has many countries close together.
Australia is the smallest continent.
Antarctica is the coldest continent and is covered in ice.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.
Asia is the largest and Australia is the smallest.
Think about it: which continent has penguins but no towns?

scenes.title: A Blue Planet
narration: From space, Earth looks blue. Why?
Oceans cover about 71 percent of the Earth.
There are five oceans.

scenes.title: Big Oceans
narration: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.
The deepest place on Earth, the Mariana Trench, is in the Pacific.
The Atlantic Ocean lies between the Americas and Europe and Africa.

scenes.title: Our Ocean and Two More
narration: The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country, India.
The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica.
The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and coldest, near the North Pole.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.
Oceans give us fish, rain and fresh air.
Think about it: how can we keep plastic out of the oceans?

scenes.title: Famous Places
narration: Some buildings are so famous that people everywhere know them.
These are called landmarks.
Let us take a trip around the world.

scenes.title: Ancient Wonders
narration: The Great Wall of China is thousands of kilometres long.
The Pyramids of Giza in Egypt were built more than 4,000 years ago.
The Taj Mahal in India is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

scenes.title: Modern Landmarks
narration: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France.
The Statue of Liberty stands in New York.
The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, built in 2018, is the tallest statue in the world.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Landmarks show what people can build together.
Each one tells the story of its country.
Think about it: which landmark would you visit first?

scenes.title: Countries as a Team
narration: What happens when countries need to solve a problem together?
They work through international organisations.
India is a member of many of them.

scenes.title: The United Nations
narration: The United Nations, or UN, was started in 1945 to keep peace in the world.
Its headquarters is in New York. India was one of its founding members.
Almost every country in the world is a member.

scenes.title: UN Helpers
narration: UNICEF helps children all over the world.
The World Health Organization, WHO, works for good health.
UNESCO looks after education, culture and heritage sites.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: These organisations help countries work as one team.
They help with peace, health, food and education.
Think about it: what problem should all countries solve together?

scenes.title: The Biggest and the Best
narration: Who decides what is the tallest, longest or fastest?
Records are measured and written in record books like Guinness World Records.
Some records are set by nature, some by people.

scenes.title: Records of Nature
narration: The Nile in Africa is usually called the longest river in the world.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth.
The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived.

scenes.title: Records by People
narration: Since 2010, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai has been the tallest building in the world.
In 2009, Usain Bolt ran 100 metres in just 9.58 seconds.
Records can be broken, so they change over time.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Nature gives us the longest, highest and biggest things.
People set records with hard work and practice.
Think about it: what record would you like to set one day?

scenes.title: Digging Up the Past
narration: What if you found a whole city buried under the ground?
That is what happened at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
They belong to the Indus Valley Civilisation, about 4,500 years old.

scenes.title: Clever City Planners
narration: Their streets were straight and crossed each other like a grid.
Houses had baked brick walls and covered drains.
Mohenjo-daro had a Great Bath for special gatherings.

scenes.title: Life and Trade
narration: People grew wheat and barley and kept animals.
They traded beads, pottery and cotton with faraway lands.
Dholavira in Gujarat, another Harappan city, became a World Heritage Site in 2021.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The Indus Valley people built some of the world's earliest planned cities.
After them came the Vedic period.
Think about it: why are clean drains important in a city?

scenes.title: Families of Kings
narration: Long ago, kings ruled India, and a family of kings is called a dynasty.
Some dynasties ruled huge kingdoms.
Let us meet a few famous ones.

scenes.title: The Mauryas and the Guptas
narration: Chandragupta Maurya started the Mauryan Empire.
His grandson Ashoka chose peace after the Kalinga war. Ashoka's lion capital is our national emblem.
The Gupta age is called a golden age of art and science. Aryabhata lived then.

scenes.title: Kingdoms of the South
narration: The Satavahanas ruled the Andhra region about 2,000 years ago.
The Cholas had a strong navy. Rajaraja Chola built the Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur.
The Kakatiyas built the Warangal Fort.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Mauryas, Guptas, Satavahanas, Cholas and Kakatiyas each left great gifts.
Temples, forts and ideas from those times still stand today.
Think about it: why did Ashoka choose peace over war?

scenes.title: The Middle Ages
narration: The time between ancient and modern India is called medieval India.
Many kingdoms rose and fell in this time.
Let us look at a few of them.

scenes.title: The Delhi Sultanate
narration: In 1206, Qutb-ud-din Aibak began the Delhi Sultanate.
He started building the Qutub Minar in Delhi.
Five dynasties ruled from Delhi during the Sultanate.

scenes.title: Kingdoms of the South and West
narration: The Vijayanagara Empire had its capital at Hampi. Krishnadevaraya was its famous king.
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj built a Maratha kingdom with strong forts.
Saints like Kabir and Mirabai sang songs of love and devotion.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Medieval India had the Sultanate, Vijayanagara, the Marathas and more.
Music, poetry and buildings grew richer in this time.
Think about it: why did kings build their forts on hills?

scenes.title: A New Empire
narration: In 1526, Babur won the First Battle of Panipat.
This began the Mughal Empire in India.
The Mughals ruled for more than 300 years.

scenes.title: Famous Mughal Emperors
narration: Akbar was known for respecting people of all religions.
Birbal and the singer Tansen were part of Akbar's court.
Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort.

scenes.title: Mughal Gifts
narration: Mughal gardens have flowing water and neat paths.
They made beautiful miniature paintings.
Aurangzeb was the last of the great Mughal emperors.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb.
They left monuments, art and gardens.
Think about it: why do you think Akbar respected all religions?

scenes.title: Traders From Far Away
narration: In 1600, the British East India Company was formed to trade with India.
They came to buy spices, cotton and silk.
Slowly, the traders began to rule.

scenes.title: Taking Control
narration: In 1757, the Company won the Battle of Plassey in Bengal.
In 1857, many Indians rose against them. It is called the First War of Independence.
After 1858, the British Crown ruled India directly.

scenes.title: Life Under British Rule
narration: The British built railways and post offices for their own needs.
Farmers paid heavy taxes, and many suffered in famines.
Indian handloom work was hurt by factory cloth from Britain.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The British came as traders and became rulers.
Their unfair rule made Indians want freedom.
Think about it: why is it important for people to rule their own country?

scenes.title: Wanting Freedom
narration: Indians wanted to rule their own land.
In 1885, the Indian National Congress was formed.
Leaders began to ask for self-rule.

scenes.title: Great Movements
narration: In 1920, Gandhiji began the Non-Cooperation Movement.
In 1930, he led the Salt March to Dandi.
In 1942, the Quit India Movement told the British to leave.

scenes.title: Many Paths to Freedom
narration: Some fought with peaceful protest, like Gandhiji.
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Indian National Army.
Women, farmers, students and workers all joined.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: On 15 August 1947, India became free.
Freedom came from the courage of millions.
Think about it: how can we thank our freedom fighters today?

scenes.title: Our Heroes
narration: Our freedom was won by many brave men and women.
Let us meet some of them.
Each one fought in their own way.

scenes.title: Leaders of the Nation
narration: Mahatma Gandhi led with truth and non-violence.
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Iron Man of India, joined the princely states into one India.
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose said, Give me blood, and I will give you freedom!

scenes.title: Brave Hearts
narration: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi fought bravely in 1857.
Bhagat Singh gave his life for freedom at just 23.
Alluri Sitarama Raju led tribal people in Andhra against British rule.
Sarojini Naidu, the Nightingale of India, was a poet and freedom fighter.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Gandhi, Patel, Netaji, Lakshmibai, Bhagat Singh, Alluri and Sarojini Naidu.
They put the country before themselves.
Think about it: which freedom fighter inspires you the most, and why?

scenes.title: A Night to Remember
narration: At midnight on 15 August 1947, India became independent.
Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister.
He gave a famous speech called Tryst with Destiny.

scenes.title: Writing Our Rules
narration: Leaders then wrote the Constitution, our book of rules.
It was adopted on 26 November 1949. We call this Constitution Day.
It came into force on 26 January 1950.

scenes.title: Becoming a Republic
narration: From that day, India became a republic, where the people choose their leaders.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first President of India.
Every year we celebrate Republic Day with a grand parade in New Delhi.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: 15 August is Independence Day, 26 January is Republic Day.
Independence gave us freedom, the Republic gave us our own rules.
Think about it: why do we sing the national anthem on these days?

scenes.title: The Rule Book of a Country
narration: A game needs rules so everyone plays fairly.
A country needs rules too. India's rules are in the Constitution.
It is the longest written constitution in the world.

scenes.title: How It Was Made
narration: The Constituent Assembly wrote it, which took nearly three years.
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the chairman of its Drafting Committee.
It came into force on 26 January 1950.

scenes.title: The Preamble
narration: The Constitution begins with the Preamble: We, the People of India.
It promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all.
It calls India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The Constitution gives us our rights and our duties.
Every law in India must follow it.
Think about it: what rule would you add to your classroom's constitution?

Indian Constitution and Government: Fund.topic: Indian Constitution and Government: Fundamental Rights
Indian Constitution and Government: Fund.title: Our Fundamental Rights

scenes.title: Rights for Everyone
narration: Some rights are so important that the Constitution protects them for every citizen.
They are called Fundamental Rights.
There are six of them.

scenes.title: The Six Rights
narration: The Right to Equality: everyone is equal before the law.
The Right to Freedom: to speak, move and work freely within the law.
The Right against Exploitation: no forced labour or child labour.
The Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

scenes.title: Right to Education
narration: Every child from 6 to 14 years has the right to free and compulsory education.
This right was made law in 2009.
If a right is taken away, people can go to the courts for help.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Equality, freedom, no exploitation, religion, culture and education, and remedies.
Rights come with duties too.
Think about it: why is the right to education so important?

Indian Constitution and Government: Fund.topic: Indian Constitution and Government: Fundamental Duties
Indian Constitution and Government: Fund.title: Our Fundamental Duties

scenes.title: Duties as Citizens
narration: If we have rights, we also have duties.
The Constitution lists 11 Fundamental Duties for every citizen.
The first ten were added to the Constitution in 1976.

scenes.title: Some of Our Duties
narration: To respect the Constitution, the national flag and the national anthem.
To protect forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife.
To keep public property safe and avoid violence.

scenes.title: More Duties
narration: To develop a scientific temper and a spirit of inquiry.
To promote harmony and brotherhood among all people.
Parents should give their children a chance to study.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Good citizens follow both their rights and their duties.
Small actions, like not littering, are duties too.
Think about it: which duty can you follow today?

scenes.title: The First Citizen
narration: The President is the head of our country and its first citizen.
The President lives in Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.
How is the President chosen?

scenes.title: Choosing the President
narration: The President is elected by members of Parliament and of the state assemblies.
The term is five years.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India.

scenes.title: What the President Does
narration: Every new law needs the President's signature.
The President is the supreme commander of the Army, Navy and Air Force.
The President appoints the Prime Minister.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The President is the head of the nation.
Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, a scientist, was President from 2002 to 2007.
Think about it: why should the President be fair to everyone?

Indian Constitution and Government: Prim.topic: Indian Constitution and Government: Prime Minister
Indian Constitution and Government: Prim.title: The Prime Minister

scenes.title: Who Runs the Government?
narration: The President is the head of the country, but who runs the government each day?
That is the Prime Minister, the head of the government.
Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister.

scenes.title: How the PM Is Chosen
narration: People vote for members of the Lok Sabha.
The leader of the party or group with the most members becomes Prime Minister.
The President appoints the Prime Minister.

scenes.title: The PM's Team
narration: The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers.
Each minister looks after a department, like education or health.
The Prime Minister speaks from the Red Fort on Independence Day.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The PM is the head of the government and leads the ministers.
Indira Gandhi, in 1966, became the first woman Prime Minister.
Think about it: if you led your class, what would you do first?

scenes.title: Where Laws Are Made
narration: Who makes the laws of our country?
The laws are made in the Parliament in New Delhi.
India moved into a new Parliament building in 2023.

scenes.title: Two Houses
narration: Parliament has the President and two houses.
The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, has members elected directly by voters.
The Rajya Sabha, or Council of States, has members chosen by the states.

scenes.title: How a Law Is Made
narration: A new idea for a law is called a bill.
Both houses discuss it and vote on it.
When the President signs it, the bill becomes a law.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and the President make up Parliament.
Members of Parliament speak for the people who chose them.
Think about it: what law would you want to make for children?

Indian Constitution and Government: Supr.topic: Indian Constitution and Government: Supreme Court
Indian Constitution and Government: Supr.title: The Supreme Court

scenes.title: The Highest Court
narration: Sometimes people disagree and need a fair judge.
The highest court in India is the Supreme Court in New Delhi.
It began work on 28 January 1950.

scenes.title: Courts at Every Level
narration: District courts handle cases in each district.
Each state or group of states has a High Court.
The Supreme Court is at the top.

scenes.title: Guardian of the Constitution
narration: The Supreme Court protects the Constitution and our rights.
It is led by the Chief Justice of India.
Its decisions must be followed all over India.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: District court, High Court, then the Supreme Court.
Courts make sure everyone gets justice.
Think about it: why must a judge listen to both sides?

Indian Constitution and Government: Stat.topic: Indian Constitution and Government: State Government
Indian Constitution and Government: Stat.title: How a State Is Run

scenes.title: A Government for Each State
narration: India is big, so each state has its own government.
It looks after things like police, roads and schools in the state.
Who leads it?

scenes.title: Leaders of the State
narration: The Governor is the head of the state and is appointed by the President.
The Chief Minister is the head of the state government.
The Chief Minister leads the state's Council of Ministers.

scenes.title: Making State Laws
narration: People elect Members of the Legislative Assembly, called MLAs.
The Legislative Assembly is also called the Vidhan Sabha.
Some states, like Andhra Pradesh, also have a Legislative Council.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Governor, Chief Minister and MLAs run the state.
The state and central governments work together.
Think about it: what would you improve in your state?

Indian Constitution and Government: Panc.topic: Indian Constitution and Government: Panchayati Raj
Indian Constitution and Government: Panc.title: Panchayati Raj

scenes.title: Villages Rule Themselves
narration: Most Indians live in villages. Who solves village problems?
The villagers choose their own local government.
This is called Panchayati Raj.

scenes.title: Three Levels
narration: The Gram Panchayat works for a village and is led by the Sarpanch.
The Panchayat Samiti, or Mandal, works for a group of villages.
The Zila Parishad works for the whole district.

scenes.title: The Gram Sabha
narration: All adult villagers together form the Gram Sabha.
It decides on wells, roads, schools and streetlights.
Panchayati Raj became part of the Constitution in 1992.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad.
We celebrate National Panchayati Raj Day on 24 April.
Think about it: what would you ask your Sarpanch to fix?

scenes.title: The Power of a Vote
narration: In a democracy, people choose their leaders.
They choose them by voting in elections.
India is the largest democracy in the world.

scenes.title: Who Votes and How
narration: Every Indian citizen aged 18 or above can vote.
Votes are cast secretly on Electronic Voting Machines.
A mark of ink on the finger shows a person has voted.

scenes.title: The Election Commission
narration: The Election Commission of India holds fair elections.
It was set up in 1950.
India's first general elections were held in 1951 and 1952.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Vote at 18, secretly and freely.
National Voters' Day is on 25 January.
Think about it: why should every adult vote?

scenes.title: A Wonderful Machine
narration: Your body is working hard even while you sleep.
Many systems work together like a team.
Let us learn some amazing facts.

scenes.title: Bones and Skin
narration: An adult human body has 206 bones.
The thigh bone, called the femur, is the longest bone.
The smallest bone, the stirrup or stapes, is inside the ear.
Skin is the largest organ of the body.

scenes.title: Heart, Lungs and Brain
narration: The heart pumps blood all day, about 70 times a minute in an adult at rest.
The lungs take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide.
The brain controls everything we think and do.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Bones hold us up, the heart pumps blood and the brain is the boss.
Good food, exercise and sleep keep the body healthy.
Think about it: which organ do you think works the hardest?

scenes.title: Looking Up
narration: People have always wondered what lies beyond the sky.
In 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space.
In 1969, Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon.

scenes.title: ISRO, Our Space Agency
narration: ISRO, the Indian Space Research Organisation, was set up in 1969.
Vikram Sarabhai is called the father of India's space programme.
India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in 1975.
In 1984, Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space.

scenes.title: Missions to the Moon and Mars
narration: Chandrayaan-1 in 2008 helped find signs of water on the Moon.
Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit in 2014, on India's very first try.
On 23 August 2023, Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: India now celebrates National Space Day on 23 August.
Space science helps with weather, maps and phones.
Think about it: what would you like to explore in space?

scenes.title: The Sun's Family
narration: The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system.
Eight planets travel around it in paths called orbits.
Can you name them in order?

scenes.title: The Planets in Order
narration: Mercury is closest to the Sun. Then come Venus, Earth and Mars.
Jupiter is the biggest planet, then Saturn with its beautiful rings.
Uranus and Neptune are the farthest icy giants.

scenes.title: Fun Facts
narration: Venus is the hottest planet, even hotter than Mercury.
Earth is the only planet known to have life.
Since 2006, Pluto has been called a dwarf planet.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles helps you remember the order.
The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
Think about it: why can't we live on Venus?

scenes.title: Science of Movement
narration: Why does a ball fall down when you throw it up?
Physics is the science of force, energy, light and sound.
Let us explore.

scenes.title: Force and Gravity
narration: A push or a pull is called a force.
Gravity is the force that pulls things towards the Earth. Isaac Newton explained it.
Friction slows things down, like when a bicycle brakes.

scenes.title: Light and Sound
narration: Light is the fastest thing we know. It travels about 3 lakh kilometres in one second.
Sound needs air, water or solids to travel, so there is no sound in space.
Magnets attract iron and have a north and a south pole.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Force, gravity, friction, light, sound and magnets are all physics.
Physics helps us build bridges, phones and rockets.
Think about it: why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?

scenes.title: What Is Everything Made Of?
narration: Everything around us is made of matter.
Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas.
Chemistry is the science of matter and how it changes.

scenes.title: Water and Air
narration: Water is made of two parts hydrogen and one part oxygen, written H2O.
The air is mostly nitrogen, about 78 percent, and about 21 percent oxygen.
We breathe in oxygen to stay alive.

scenes.title: Changes Around Us
narration: Sugar dissolves in water to make a solution.
Iron rusts when it meets air and water.
Lemon juice is an acid and soap is a base. Never taste chemicals to test them!

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Solids, liquids and gases change into one another.
Chemistry is at work when we cook, clean and grow plants.
Think about it: what happens to ice cream on a hot day?

scenes.title: What Is Alive?
narration: A plant, a dog and you are all living things.
Biology is the science of living things.
What are living things made of?

scenes.title: Cells
narration: All living things are made of tiny cells.
In 1665, Robert Hooke first saw cells using a microscope.
Your body has trillions of cells.

scenes.title: Plants and Animals
narration: Green plants make their own food from sunlight. This is photosynthesis.
Animals eat plants or other animals. This forms a food chain.
Jagadish Chandra Bose showed that plants respond to the world around them.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Cells, plants, animals and food chains are part of biology.
Biology helps doctors and farmers.
Think about it: what would happen if there were no plants?

scenes.title: Curious Minds
narration: Every great discovery begins with a question.
Scientists find answers by observing and testing.
Let us meet some famous scientists.

scenes.title: Scientists of the World
narration: Isaac Newton explained gravity and motion.
Albert Einstein changed how we understand light, time and space.
Marie Curie studied radioactivity and won two Nobel Prizes.

scenes.title: Scientists of India
narration: C. V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for the Raman Effect.
We celebrate National Science Day on 28 February for his discovery.
Srinivasa Ramanujan was a genius of numbers. National Mathematics Day is on 22 December.
Homi Bhabha led India's atomic research.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Newton, Einstein, Curie, Raman, Ramanujan and Bhabha.
Scientists never stop asking why.
Think about it: what question would you like to answer as a scientist?

scenes.title: A Clever Idea
narration: An invention is a new thing made to solve a problem.
The wheel was one of the first great inventions.
Ancient Indian mathematicians gave the world the idea of zero.

scenes.title: Inventions We Use
narration: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, around 1440, made books easy to print.
Alexander Graham Bell got a patent for the telephone in 1876.
Thomas Edison made a long-lasting electric bulb in 1879.

scenes.title: Flying and More
narration: In 1903, the Wright brothers flew the first powered aeroplane.
Medicines and vaccines save millions of lives.
Computers and the internet changed how we learn and talk.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Wheel, zero, printing press, telephone, bulb and aeroplane.
Inventors keep trying even when they fail.
Think about it: what would you invent to help your school?

scenes.title: A Smart Machine
narration: A computer is a machine that follows instructions very fast.
Charles Babbage is called the father of the computer.
Computers understand only two digits, 0 and 1.

scenes.title: Parts of a Computer
narration: We give input with a keyboard and a mouse.
The CPU is the brain of the computer.
We see output on a monitor or from a printer.

scenes.title: Hardware and Software
narration: Parts you can touch are called hardware.
Programs and apps are called software.
Memory, like RAM, holds work while the computer is on.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Input, processing in the CPU, then output.
Computers help in schools, hospitals, banks and space missions.
Think about it: what would you like a computer to help you learn?

scenes.title: A Web Around the World
narration: The internet connects millions of computers all over the world.
It lets us send messages, watch videos and learn.
In 1989, Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web.

scenes.title: The Internet in India
narration: Public internet service began in India on 15 August 1995.
Today we use the internet for online classes and digital payments.
Email lets us send letters in seconds.

scenes.title: Staying Safe Online
narration: Never share your password, address or photos with strangers.
If something online makes you uneasy, tell a trusted adult.
Not everything on the internet is true, so check with good sources.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The internet connects the world and helps us learn.
Be kind and careful online.
Think about it: how can you tell if a website is trustworthy?

Science and Technology: AI and Robotics.topic: Science and Technology: AI and Robotics
Science and Technology: AI and Robotics.title: Smart Machines: AI and Robots

scenes.title: Machines That Learn
narration: Can a computer learn like we do?
Artificial Intelligence, or AI, lets computers learn from examples.
AI helps maps find the fastest road and apps translate languages.

scenes.title: Robots
narration: A robot is a machine that can do tasks by itself.
Robots build cars in factories and explore Mars.
ISRO made a humanoid robot named Vyommitra for its human space mission.

scenes.title: Using AI Wisely
narration: AI can make mistakes, so people must check its answers.
AI should help people and be fair to everyone.
This app uses AI to make lessons for you!

scenes.title: Recap
narration: AI learns patterns, robots do tasks.
Humans stay in charge of smart machines.
Think about it: what job would you give a helpful robot?

scenes.title: Living Together
narration: In a pond, fish, frogs, plants, water and sunlight all work together.
Living and non-living things together make an ecosystem.
Every ecosystem is a team.

scenes.title: Producers, Consumers and Decomposers
narration: Plants are producers. They make food using sunlight.
Animals are consumers. They eat plants or other animals.
Fungi and bacteria are decomposers. They break down dead things into soil.

scenes.title: Kinds of Ecosystems
narration: Forests, deserts, grasslands, ponds and oceans are ecosystems.
The Sundarbans is a mangrove ecosystem with tigers that can swim.
A change in one part affects the whole ecosystem.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Producers, consumers and decomposers keep nature in balance.
People are part of ecosystems too.
Think about it: what lives in the ecosystem near your home?

scenes.title: So Many Living Things
narration: From tiny ants to huge elephants, Earth is full of life.
The variety of all living things is called biodiversity.
Why is it important?

scenes.title: India Is Special
narration: India is one of the most biodiverse countries in the world.
The Western Ghats and the Himalayas are biodiversity hotspots.
India has tigers, elephants, rhinos, lions and peacocks.

scenes.title: Protecting Biodiversity
narration: Project Tiger began in 1973 to save tigers.
Cutting forests and pollution put many species in danger.
International Day for Biological Diversity is on 22 May.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Every plant and animal has a role in nature.
More biodiversity makes nature stronger.
Think about it: how many kinds of birds can you spot near your home?

scenes.title: Weather and Climate
narration: Weather is what it is like outside today.
Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years.
Earth's climate is now changing faster than before.

scenes.title: Why It Is Changing
narration: Burning coal, petrol and diesel adds gases to the air.
Cutting down forests means fewer trees to clean the air.
These gases trap heat, making Earth warmer.

scenes.title: What Happens
narration: Glaciers melt and sea levels rise.
Some places get more floods, others more droughts.
In 2015, countries signed the Paris Agreement to fight climate change.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Climate change is a long-term change in Earth's weather.
Saving energy and planting trees help.
Think about it: what can your family do to save energy?

scenes.title: A Warm Blanket
narration: On a cold night, a blanket keeps you warm.
Some gases in the air act like a blanket around the Earth.
They are called greenhouse gases.

scenes.title: Too Thick a Blanket
narration: Carbon dioxide is the main greenhouse gas.
Burning fuels adds more of it, making the blanket thicker.
So Earth's average temperature goes up. This is global warming.

scenes.title: What We Can Do
narration: Trees take in carbon dioxide, so plant more of them.
Walk, cycle or use buses instead of cars when possible.
Switch off lights and fans when you leave a room.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: More greenhouse gases mean a warmer Earth.
Small actions by many people make a big difference.
Think about it: how many lights in your home could be switched off right after use?

scenes.title: Dirty Air, Water and Land
narration: When harmful things get into nature, it is called pollution.
It can harm people, animals and plants.
There are four main kinds.

scenes.title: Four Kinds of Pollution
narration: Air pollution comes from smoke from vehicles, factories and burning waste.
Water pollution happens when waste is dumped into rivers and lakes.
Soil pollution comes from plastic and too many chemicals.
Noise pollution comes from loud horns and speakers.

scenes.title: Fighting Pollution
narration: The Namami Gange programme began in 2014 to clean the Ganga.
Using less plastic and dustbins for waste helps.
Cleaner fuels and electric vehicles reduce smoke.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Air, water, soil and noise pollution.
A cleaner world starts with each of us.
Think about it: what makes noise pollution near your school?

scenes.title: Energy That Never Runs Out
narration: Coal and petrol will run out one day.
Sunlight, wind and flowing water never run out.
Energy from them is called renewable energy.

scenes.title: Kinds of Renewable Energy
narration: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.
Windmills turn the wind into electricity.
Dams use falling water to make hydroelectric power.
Biogas is made from cow dung and kitchen waste.

scenes.title: India Goes Green
narration: Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan is one of the largest solar parks in the world.
In 2015, India and France started the International Solar Alliance.
Clean energy causes much less pollution.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Sun, wind, water and biogas give clean energy.
Saving energy is just as important as making it.
Think about it: where could you put solar panels at your school?

scenes.title: Saving for Tomorrow
narration: Conservation means using nature wisely so it lasts.
We protect forests, water, animals and soil.
People in India have a long history of caring for nature.

scenes.title: Famous Efforts
narration: In 1973, villagers in the Chipko Movement hugged trees to stop them being cut.
Project Tiger also began in 1973 and helped tiger numbers grow.
Van Mahotsav, a tree-planting festival, is held in the first week of July.

scenes.title: Saving Water
narration: Rainwater harvesting collects rain to use later.
Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
Reduce, reuse and recycle to save resources.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Conservation protects nature for children in the future.
Every small step counts.
Think about it: how could your class save water this week?

scenes.title: A Big Idea
narration: We need homes, roads and factories. But we also need clean air and forests.
Sustainable development means meeting today's needs without harming the future.
How can we do both?

scenes.title: The Global Goals
narration: In 2015, the United Nations agreed on 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
They include no poverty, zero hunger, good health and quality education.
Countries aim to reach these goals by 2030.

scenes.title: Living Sustainably
narration: Use things again instead of throwing them away.
Choose clean energy and save electricity.
Share and do not waste food.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Sustainable means good for people today and tomorrow.
Everyone can help reach the global goals.
Think about it: which global goal matters most to you?

scenes.title: The Biggest Sports Festival
narration: Every four years, athletes from around the world meet for the Olympic Games.
The first Olympics were held long ago in Olympia, in ancient Greece.
The modern Olympics began in Athens in 1896.

scenes.title: Symbols of the Olympics
narration: The five rings stand for the continents joined together in sport.
The Olympic flame is carried by runners in a torch relay.
The motto is Faster, Higher, Stronger, Together.

scenes.title: India at the Olympics
narration: India's hockey team has won eight Olympic gold medals.
In 2008, Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual gold, in shooting.
Neeraj Chopra won gold in javelin at the Tokyo Games, held in 2021.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Gold, silver and bronze medals go to the top three.
The Paralympics are held for athletes with disabilities.
Think about it: which Olympic sport would you like to play?

scenes.title: Champions of the World
narration: A World Cup decides the best team in the world in a sport.
Teams play many matches to reach the final.
Let us look at some famous World Cups.

scenes.title: Cricket World Cups
narration: The first Cricket World Cup was played in 1975.
India won it in 1983 under Kapil Dev and in 2011 under M. S. Dhoni.
India won the T20 World Cup in 2007 and again in 2024.

scenes.title: Football and Hockey
narration: The FIFA World Cup in football began in 1930 in Uruguay.
It is held every four years and watched by billions of people.
India won the Hockey World Cup in 1975.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Cricket, football and hockey all have World Cups.
Teamwork wins World Cups.
Think about it: why does a team need every player to do well?

scenes.title: Asia's Big Games
narration: The Asian Games are a sports festival for countries of Asia.
They are held every four years.
The very first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.

scenes.title: Many Sports
narration: Athletes compete in running, wrestling, kabaddi, badminton and more.
Kabaddi, an Indian sport, is part of the Asian Games.
India hosted the Games again in 1982.

scenes.title: A Record Year
narration: The Asian Games in Hangzhou, China, were held in 2023.
India won more than 100 medals there for the first time.
The athletes worked hard for years to win.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The Asian Games began in Delhi in 1951.
They bring the people of Asia together through sport.
Think about it: what sport would you choose to win a medal in?

scenes.title: Champions Who Inspire
narration: Sports stars show us what practice and courage can do.
Let us meet some famous athletes.
Each one worked for years to become a champion.

scenes.title: Indian Heroes
narration: Milkha Singh, the Flying Sikh, was a great runner.
P. T. Usha, the Payyoli Express, ran in many Olympic races.
Mary Kom became world boxing champion six times.
P. V. Sindhu won Olympic medals in badminton in 2016 and 2021.

scenes.title: World Heroes
narration: Sachin Tendulkar scored 100 international centuries in cricket.
Usain Bolt of Jamaica is famous as the fastest sprinter.
Viswanathan Anand was India's first chess Grandmaster, in 1988.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Hard work, discipline and never giving up make champions.
Champions also respect their opponents.
Think about it: which sports hero inspires you, and why?

scenes.title: Breaking Records
narration: A record is the best result ever achieved in something.
Records are written down with the year they were set.
Records can be broken by future athletes.

scenes.title: Amazing Records
narration: In 2009, Usain Bolt ran 100 metres in 9.58 seconds.
Michael Phelps won 23 Olympic gold medals in swimming.
Sachin Tendulkar is the only player with 100 international centuries in cricket.

scenes.title: Indian Records
narration: In 2014, Rohit Sharma scored 264 runs in a single one-day international.
India's hockey team won six Olympic golds in a row, from 1928 to 1956.
In 2024, D. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world chess champion.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Records show how far practice can take us.
Always check the year, because records change.
Think about it: what personal record would you like to break?

Sports: Sports Terminology.title: Words From the World of Sport

scenes.title: Every Sport Has Its Words
narration: Players and fans use special words in each sport.
Knowing them helps you enjoy the game.
Let us learn some.

scenes.title: Cricket and Football
narration: In cricket, an over has six balls, and 100 runs is a century.
A wicket falls when a batter is out.
In football, a penalty is a free kick at goal from a set spot.

scenes.title: Tennis, Hockey and Chess
narration: In tennis, love means zero, and an ace is a serve the other player cannot touch.
In hockey, a penalty corner is a special attack from the goal line.
In chess, checkmate means the king is trapped and the game ends. Chess began in India as chaturanga.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Over, century, wicket, penalty, love, ace and checkmate.
Every sport has fair-play rules.
Think about it: which sports word do you use most?

scenes.title: Writers Who Shape Our World
narration: Authors write stories, poems and books that we love.
Some books are enjoyed for hundreds of years.
Let us meet some famous writers.

scenes.title: Indian Authors
narration: Rabindranath Tagore wrote Gitanjali and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
Tagore also wrote our national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
R. K. Narayan wrote stories set in the town of Malgudi.
Ruskin Bond writes stories about the hills of Mussoorie.

scenes.title: More Great Writers
narration: Munshi Premchand wrote famous stories in Hindi and Urdu.
William Shakespeare wrote plays like Romeo and Juliet.
J. K. Rowling wrote the Harry Potter books.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Tagore was the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize, in 1913.
Reading great authors makes us better writers.
Think about it: who is your favourite author?

scenes.title: Books Are Windows
narration: A book can take you to faraway lands without leaving home.
Some books are loved by every generation.
Let us look at some famous books.

scenes.title: Ancient Indian Books
narration: The Panchatantra by Vishnu Sharma has animal stories that teach lessons.
The Ramayana was written by Valmiki.
The Mahabharata was written by Vyasa.

scenes.title: Modern Books
narration: The Jungle Book by Rudyard Kipling tells the story of Mowgli.
Wings of Fire is the life story of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.
The Discovery of India was written by Jawaharlal Nehru while he was in prison.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Panchatantra, Ramayana, Mahabharata, Jungle Book, Wings of Fire.
A few pages every day builds a reading habit.
Think about it: what lesson did your favourite story teach you?

scenes.title: Words With Music
narration: A poem uses words with rhythm and often rhyme.
Poems help us feel joy, sadness or wonder.
Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star was written by Jane Taylor in 1806.

scenes.title: Great Indian Poems
narration: Vande Mataram, our national song, was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
Tagore wrote Where the Mind is Without Fear, a poem about a free India.
Subhadra Kumari Chauhan's poem Jhansi ki Rani honours Rani Lakshmibai.

scenes.title: The Nightingale of India
narration: Sarojini Naidu was called the Nightingale of India.
She wrote In the Bazaars of Hyderabad about colourful markets.
Poets use pictures in words, like as bright as the Sun.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Rhythm, rhyme and feeling make a poem.
Reading poems aloud makes them come alive.
Think about it: what would you write a poem about?

Literature and Arts: Indian Classical Da.topic: Literature and Arts: Indian Classical Dances
Literature and Arts: Indian Classical Da.title: Classical Dances of India

scenes.title: Stories Through Dance
narration: In classical dance, dancers tell stories with steps, hands and faces.
Hand gestures are called mudras.
India has eight recognised classical dance forms.

scenes.title: Dances of the South
narration: Bharatanatyam comes from Tamil Nadu.
Kuchipudi comes from a village of the same name in Andhra Pradesh.
Kathakali and Mohiniyattam come from Kerala.

scenes.title: Dances of the North and East
narration: Kathak is from North India and is known for fast spins and footwork.
Odissi is from Odisha, and Manipuri is from Manipur.
Sattriya comes from Assam.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Kathak, Odissi, Manipuri and Sattriya.
Each dance shows the culture of its region.
Think about it: which dance would you like to learn?

scenes.title: Sounds of India
narration: Music is made with voices and instruments.
Instruments can be played by plucking, beating or blowing.
Let us hear some Indian instruments.

scenes.title: Strings and Drums
narration: The sitar and the veena are string instruments.
Pandit Ravi Shankar made the sitar famous around the world.
The tabla and the mridangam are drums. Zakir Hussain was a world-famous tabla player.

scenes.title: Wind Instruments
narration: The bansuri is a bamboo flute. Hariprasad Chaurasia is a flute master.
The shehnai is played at weddings and festivals.
Ustad Bismillah Khan, a shehnai maestro, received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Sitar and veena for strings, tabla and mridangam for drums, bansuri and shehnai for wind.
Music brings people together.
Think about it: what instrument would you like to play?

scenes.title: Pictures That Tell Stories
narration: A painting can show a feeling, a story or a moment.
Some paintings are treasured all over the world.
Let us visit a gallery.

scenes.title: World-Famous Paintings
narration: The Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci hangs in the Louvre museum in Paris.
The Starry Night by Vincent van Gogh shows a swirling night sky.
The Ajanta caves have paintings more than 1,500 years old.

scenes.title: Indian Art
narration: Raja Ravi Varma painted scenes from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.
Bharat Mata by Abanindranath Tagore became a symbol of the freedom movement.
Madhubani from Bihar and Warli from Maharashtra are famous folk art styles.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Mona Lisa, The Starry Night, Ajanta and Bharat Mata.
Art helps us understand history and feelings.
Think about it: what would you paint about your town?

scenes.title: People Who Create
narration: Artists create paintings, statues and designs.
They see the world in their own special way.
Let us meet some great artists.

scenes.title: Artists of India
narration: Raja Ravi Varma made paintings that were printed and loved in homes.
Amrita Sher-Gil painted the lives of Indian women.
Nandalal Bose decorated the original copy of the Constitution of India.

scenes.title: Artists of the World
narration: Leonardo da Vinci was a painter, scientist and inventor.
Pablo Picasso painted in bold new shapes.
Kalamkari is a hand-painted cloth art from Andhra Pradesh.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Ravi Varma, Amrita Sher-Gil, Nandalal Bose, Leonardo and Picasso.
Every child can be an artist.
Think about it: what colours would you use to paint happiness?

Business and Economy: Money and Currency.topic: Business and Economy: Money and Currency
Business and Economy: Money and Currency.title: Money and Currency

scenes.title: Before Money
narration: Long ago, people swapped things they had for things they needed.
This swapping was called barter.
But barter was hard. What if nobody wanted your rice?

scenes.title: Coins and Notes
narration: So people began using coins and then paper notes.
In India, the Reserve Bank of India issues our notes.
The rupee symbol ₹ was adopted in 2010.

scenes.title: Digital Money
narration: Today many people pay with phones and cards.
UPI, started in 2016, lets people pay instantly by phone.
Always keep your PIN secret.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Barter, coins, notes and now digital money.
Money helps us buy, sell and save.
Think about it: why is money easier than barter?

scenes.title: A Safe Place for Money
narration: Where should you keep money safely?
A bank keeps people's money safe.
The bank also pays a little extra money, called interest, on savings.

scenes.title: Services of a Bank
narration: A savings account helps people save.
Banks give loans to help people build houses or start businesses.
ATMs let people take out cash anytime.

scenes.title: The Bank of Banks
narration: The Reserve Bank of India is India's central bank.
It was set up in 1935, and its headquarters is now in Mumbai.
It looks after all other banks and India's money supply.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Banks keep money safe, pay interest and give loans.
A passbook or app shows how much money is in an account.
Think about it: why do banks pay interest on savings?

scenes.title: A Piggy Bank
narration: When you put coins in a piggy bank, you are saving.
Saving means keeping some money for later.
Why should we save?

scenes.title: Needs and Wants
narration: Needs are things we must have, like food and school books.
Wants are things that are nice to have, like toys.
Smart savers pay for needs first.

scenes.title: Making Savings Grow
narration: Money saved in a bank earns interest, so it grows.
Making a budget means planning how to spend and save.
Saving a little every week adds up to a lot.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Save some, spend wisely on needs first.
Savings help in emergencies and for big goals.
Think about it: what would you save up for?

scenes.title: Who Pays for Roads?
narration: Who pays for the roads, schools and hospitals we all use?
The government pays, using money called taxes.
People and businesses pay taxes to the government.

scenes.title: Kinds of Taxes
narration: Income tax is paid on the money people earn.
GST is a tax added when we buy many goods and services.
GST started in India on 1 July 2017.

scenes.title: How Taxes Help
narration: Taxes pay for police, soldiers and firefighters.
They build bridges and provide free school meals.
Paying taxes honestly is a duty of every citizen.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Taxes are our shared money for things we all use.
Income tax and GST are two kinds.
Think about it: what should tax money build in your town?

Business and Economy: Imports and Export.topic: Business and Economy: Imports and Exports
Business and Economy: Imports and Export.title: Trade With the World

scenes.title: Buying and Selling Across Borders
narration: Countries buy and sell things with each other. This is trade.
Selling things to other countries is called exporting.
Buying things from other countries is called importing.

scenes.title: What India Trades
narration: India exports software services, medicines, rice, spices and gems.
India imports crude oil, gold and electronic parts.
Ships carry goods through busy ports like Mumbai, Chennai and Visakhapatnam.

scenes.title: Why Trade Matters
narration: No country can make everything it needs.
Trade creates jobs and helps businesses grow.
Exports earn money from other countries for India.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Export means selling out, import means buying in.
Trade connects India with the world.
Think about it: can you find something at home that was imported?

scenes.title: Where Things Are Made
narration: An industry makes goods or provides services.
Industries give jobs to millions of people.
Let us visit some big industries of India.

scenes.title: Making Things
narration: The textile industry makes cloth. Surat is famous for textiles and diamond cutting.
Jamshedpur is known for iron and steel. Tata Steel was started there in 1907.
Chennai makes so many cars that it is called the Detroit of Asia.

scenes.title: Services and Medicines
narration: Bengaluru and Hyderabad are centres of the IT industry.
Hyderabad makes many medicines and vaccines.
Agriculture-based industries make sugar, tea and food products.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Textiles, steel, cars, IT and medicines.
Industries help India grow.
Think about it: what industry is near your town?

scenes.title: Big Ideas, Big Companies
narration: A company is a group of people working together to make or sell something.
Some Indian companies started small and grew very big.
Let us learn about a few.

scenes.title: Old and Famous
narration: Jamsetji Tata founded the Tata group, which built India's first big steel plant.
Amul began in Anand, Gujarat, as a cooperative owned by milk farmers.
Verghese Kurien, the Milkman of India, led the White Revolution with Amul.

scenes.title: New Age Companies
narration: Infosys, started in 1981, became a big software company.
Indian Railways is one of the biggest employers in the world. It is run by the government.
Many young Indians now start new companies called start-ups.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Companies grow with good ideas and hard work.
Cooperatives like Amul help farmers share profits.
Think about it: what company would you start one day?

scenes.title: Following the News
narration: News tells us what is happening in our country.
Some events make the whole nation proud.
News changes every day, so read it with your family.

scenes.title: Recent Proud Moments
narration: On 23 August 2023, Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole.
In September 2023, India hosted the G20 Summit in New Delhi.
In 2023, India's new Parliament building was opened.

scenes.title: Every Year
narration: Every 26 January, a grand Republic Day parade is held on Kartavya Path in New Delhi.
On Independence Day, the flag is hoisted at the Red Fort.
In 2022, India celebrated 75 years of independence.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Always remember the year of each event.
Newspapers and news channels help us stay informed.
Think about it: what good news about India did you hear this week?

scenes.title: One World
narration: Events in one country can affect the whole world.
Leaders meet to talk about problems we all share.
Let us look at some important world events.

scenes.title: Big Gatherings
narration: At the G20 Summit in New Delhi in 2023, the African Union joined the G20.
Every September, world leaders meet at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Every year, countries meet at climate talks called COP to fight climate change.

scenes.title: Sports and Science
narration: The Summer Olympics were held in Paris in 2024.
In 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched to look deep into space.
News changes every day, so check new reports with an adult.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: The G20, the UN, climate talks and the Olympics bring the world together.
Every event has a year. Learn it with the event.
Think about it: which world problem should countries solve together?

scenes.title: Science Never Stops
narration: Scientists keep finding new things about our world and space.
Let us look at some discoveries from recent years.
Each discovery helps us learn more.

scenes.title: India in Space
narration: In 2023, Chandrayaan-3's rover Pragyan found sulphur near the Moon's south pole.
In 2023, India launched Aditya-L1 to study the Sun.
In January 2024, Aditya-L1 reached its viewing spot in space.

scenes.title: Around the World
narration: The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, takes pictures of very old galaxies.
Vaccines made very quickly helped fight COVID-19 in 2020 and 2021.
Scientists use AI to help discover new medicines.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Aditya-L1, Chandrayaan-3 and James Webb taught us new things.
New discoveries come every year, so keep reading science news.
Think about it: what mystery of space would you like solved?

scenes.title: Big Sports Moments
narration: Sports events fill the news with exciting moments.
Let us remember some recent big events.
Records and winners change, so always note the year.

scenes.title: 2024 Highlights
narration: In 2024, India won the T20 Cricket World Cup.
At the 2024 Paris Olympics, India won six medals.
Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals in shooting at Paris 2024.

scenes.title: Chess and More
narration: In 2024, India won both the open and women's gold at the Chess Olympiad.
In December 2024, D. Gukesh became world chess champion at age 18.
In 2023, Neeraj Chopra became the javelin world champion.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: T20 World Cup, Paris Olympics and chess gold were big moments in 2024.
Follow sports news to learn about new champions.
Think about it: which sports event would you like to watch live?

scenes.title: Honouring Great Work
narration: Awards honour people who do outstanding work.
Some are given in India, some by the world.
New winners are announced every year.

scenes.title: Indian Awards
narration: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award.
In 2024, it was given to five people, including the farm scientist M. S. Swaminathan.
Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri are announced on Republic Day eve.

scenes.title: World Awards
narration: The Nobel Prizes are announced every October.
The Nobel Peace Prize honours people who work for peace.
Sports stars receive the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, India's top sports award.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Bharat Ratna, Padma Awards, Khel Ratna and Nobel Prizes.
Always learn the year along with the winner's name.
Think about it: who in your town deserves an award, and why?

scenes.title: Plans for a Better India
narration: The government starts missions to solve big problems.
Each mission has a name and a goal.
Let us learn about some of them.

scenes.title: Missions for Everyone
narration: Swachh Bharat Mission, started in 2014, works for a clean India.
Digital India, started in 2015, brings services online.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, started in 2015, helps girls study and stay safe.

scenes.title: Water, Food and Making Things
narration: Jal Jeevan Mission, started in 2019, aims to bring tap water to every rural home.
PM POSHAN gives hot meals to children in government schools.
Make in India, started in 2014, encourages making goods in India.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Clean India, Digital India, girls' education, tap water and school meals.
Missions succeed when people take part.
Think about it: how can you help the Swachh Bharat Mission?

scenes.title: Caring for Earth
narration: News often talks about our forests, rivers and wildlife.
Many new efforts aim to protect nature.
Let us look at some from recent years.

scenes.title: Saving Animals
narration: In September 2022, cheetahs were brought from Namibia to Kuno National Park.
Cheetahs had disappeared from India about 70 years before that.
Project Tiger has helped India become home to most of the world's wild tigers.

scenes.title: Green Habits
narration: In 2024, the Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam campaign asked people to plant a tree for their mother.
Mission LiFE asks people to live in planet-friendly ways.
Heatwaves and floods in the news remind us to protect the climate.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Project Cheetah, tree planting and Mission LiFE are green steps.
Each of us can save water, energy and trees.
Think about it: what green habit can your family start?

Current Affairs: Important People and Ac.topic: Current Affairs: Important People and Achievements
Current Affairs: Important People and Ac.title: Indians Who Made Us Proud

scenes.title: Proud Moments
narration: Some people do things that make the whole country proud.
Their stories teach us courage and hard work.
Let us meet a few from recent years.

scenes.title: Firsts and Records
narration: In 2022, Droupadi Murmu became the first tribal woman President of India.
In 2023, ISRO's team landed Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon's south pole.
In 2024, D. Gukesh became the youngest world chess champion.

scenes.title: Sports Stars
narration: Neeraj Chopra won Olympic gold in 2021 and the world title in 2023.
Avani Lekhara won Paralympic shooting gold in 2021 and again in 2024.
Manu Bhaker won two Olympic medals at one Games in 2024.

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Hard work and courage take people to great heights.
Always remember the year of each achievement.
Think about it: what achievement would you like to be known for?
